summary: This was an open seat because Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis was term-limited. Republican Byron Donalds, a U.S. representative, won, defeating Democrat David Jolly.

candidates.name: Byron Donalds
candidates.bio: Byron Donalds is a Republican who represents Florida's 19th congressional district in the U.S. House. He was elected to the Florida House of Representatives in 2016 and previously worked in banking, finance and insurance in Southwest Florida. He grew up in Brooklyn, New York.

positions.summary: Says he would keep property taxes in check, cut permitting red tape, and lower homeowners insurance costs by curbing lawsuit abuse and keeping Citizens Insurance small.
Says his plan would require posted cash prices for the 50 most common procedures and require insurers to approve common treatments within three days.
Says he would require E-Verify for all Florida businesses and have state and local police work with federal authorities to deport noncitizens who commit crimes.
Says he would let education funding follow the student so parents can choose schools, and would provide free tutoring for struggling third graders.

candidates.name: David Jolly
candidates.bio: David Jolly is a Democrat who represented Florida's 13th congressional district in the U.S. House as a Republican from 2014 to 2017. He left the Republican Party in 2018 and registered as a Democrat in April 2025. He is an attorney and former lobbyist.

positions.summary: Has called for raising teacher pay by 30%, a 10-year "renaissance" for public education, and limiting voucher eligibility by income.
Describes himself as pro-choice and proposes replacing Florida's six-week ban with a law allowing abortion until fetal viability.
Says Florida should value its immigrant community, rejects linking immigration to crime, and supports a more streamlined path to documented status.

Proposes a state catastrophe fund to move hurricane risk out of the private insurance market, which he says could cut residential property insurance costs by 60%, and supports major property tax reform that does not repeal Save Our Homes.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (MultiState governors tracker, updated Nov 4, 35 of 36 races called). Shares checked on November 25, 2026 against The Green Papers (8,271,627 votes in total), which does not say the count is certified.
